react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged on a single dominant biological signal: steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150 (both named 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism') at rank 1 with FDR 5.7e-15 and fold-enrichment 1429.7, hitting 5 of 7 input metabolites. Mummichog's empirical-compound network scored the corresponding KEGG-equivalent pathway at rank 0 (p 8.4e-05) with an extraordinary 11/11 overlap — every compound in the Mummichog module matched the input list. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 ('C21-Steroid Hormone Biosynthesis and Metabolism') as the sole significant hit (p 8.391e-06), capturing the same 5 steroid ligands. The five driver metabolites are testosterone (KEGG:C00535), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), DHEA (KEGG:C01227), estradiol (KEGG:C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917), all confirmed as pathway members via the EnrichmentResult metabolites_hit rosters. Androstenedione occupies the branchpoint position, serving as the direct precursor for both testosterone (via HSD17B3) and estrone (via aromatase), making it the most central node in the differential set. The remaining two input compounds — butanone (KEGG:C02845) and sulindac (KEGG:C01531) — did not participate in the steroid pathway hits; sulindac surfaced in a separate m/z-direct xenobiotics hit (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism, rank 2, p 0.029), consistent with its NSAID chemical scaffold. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed zero structural conflicts across all seven input identifiers. The treatment group perturbation strongly implicates the C21 steroid hormone biosynthesis axis, with aromatase and 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase steps as the most plausible enzymatic sites of differential activity.
